### RULING 241 — Level 1 activation parameters: a TEMPORARY $25/day rolling research spend ceiling, the local dispatchOne worker runtime, hosted worker runtimes deferred to the frontier

*2026-09-01 · author_explicit · `R-0241`*

**The daily research model-spend ceiling is $25 per rolling 24 hours.** It is
recorded as a TEMPORARY ACTIVATION SAFETY CEILING for owner adjustment, not as
business policy. When the ceiling is reached, the remaining Scout work stays
durably owed with its next-due — deferred, never dropped, never reported
complete. The cap controls how much work runs and never whether a fact is true.

**The worker runtime for this activation is the existing local `dispatchOne`
path on the standing runner**, over the Playwright and network infrastructure
already in the repository. Hosted worker runtimes — managed agent services —
are FRONTIER, not authorized here.

The code constants live in `lib/control-plane/scheduler/research-policy.ts`
(`RESEARCH_BOUNDS`) and are named there, never here.

## rendering-neutrality

### RULING 123 — the author's decisions of 2026-08-24, recorded as a batch

*2026-08-24 · author_explicit · `R-0123`*


*Adopted 2026-08-24 (Sean's decisions of that day, given in the session brief and in a mid-session correction). Law: none of it — these are decisions, not rules, which is exactly what this file is for. Supersedes nothing.*

**Not every decision is a rule.** Most of what an author decides is a call about one thing on one day: this photograph ships, that one does not, this gate is the right shape, that document is the copy to use. Those decisions bind just as firmly as a rule does and they belong written down, because a decision that lives only in a chat window is one nobody can check later — which is the whole reason this file exists.

This entry records the ones Sean made on 2026-08-24 that are not rules. The five that ARE rules became RULINGS 117 through 122 and have their own entries.

**The photographs — all approved.**

- **The seven Morris County commissioner portraits.** All seven from the county's own site, all seven read as images. Six shipped; the seventh was already shipping.
- **The five New Jersey municipal portraits** — Rowland, Senatore, Mabey, Althoff, Muilenburg — each from the municipality's own website. Two carried stated reservations and he approved them with the reservations in view: Senatore's attribution is by POSITION on the page rather than by filename, and Mabey's is full-length rather than head-and-shoulders.
- **The three New Hampshire county portraits** — Hagaman, Raiche, Ribas.
- **The two campaign portraits at 07866** — Leguía and Hathaway. Hathaway's was put to him as a three-quarter-length shot rather than a portrait, stated as a reservation, and he took it.
- **The forty-eight that were already shipping**, approved EN BLOC. In his words: he checked a few, and if one has issues later he will call it out specifically; otherwise good to go. They had been recorded as "grandfathered", which meant shipping before the rule existed and approved by nobody. They are his now. **The record says en bloc rather than per asset**, because that is what happened, and writing it the other way would claim he read forty-eight images one at a time.

**Tobin Menard stays initials.** His campaign publishes exactly one picture of him and it carries the words "Accountability Responsibility" printed across it. His words: *no campaign slogans or anything like that.* The refusal is affirmed. He renders honest initials, which this product treats as a success, and the hunt for a clean portrait of him continues.

**The other decisions of the day.**

- **The meetings refresh gates per source, not per run** — one broken source may not throw away the work of the healthy ones. His condition: the broken source carries forward and is loudly identified for fixing.
- **The demo-deletion promise is built**, with the wall coming down as the trigger: rows collected during the password-walled test period delete when the wall lifts, and the deletion is logged.
- **The session map, the intent document and the rebuilt tracker sections are confirmed** — the committed copies are the ones to use.
- **The candidate questionnaire is on HOLD.** He reviews the instrument and the invitation before anything sends. Nothing has been sent to anybody.
- **The agenda-platform crawler is re-scoped rather than shelved**: it starts after the pilot zips are done rather than after the election, and its open design questions come to him before the first fetch.
- **The Census API key was activated**, mid-session. It had been refused by the host as invalid; it now answers with real data.

*Why one entry rather than a dozen.* These were given together, on one day, in one brief. Splitting them into separate numbered rulings would suggest each was reasoned about separately and would make the record longer without making it truer.

## shipping-ci

### RULING 213 — no external orchestration service; the scheduler builds on the existing control-plane interfaces

*2026-08-30 · author_explicit · `R-0213`*

No external orchestration service (Temporal or equivalent). The scheduler
builds on the EXISTING provider-neutral control-plane repository interfaces —
one control plane, never a second one built beside it. The runtime persistence
provider for Level-2 scheduling authority (the existing filesystem provider
versus a Postgres-backed provider implementing the same interfaces) is an
explicit decision recorded by this session (RULING 220) with a
migration/adapter plan; it is never resolved by silently re-implementing state
elsewhere. The revisit trigger for external orchestration: a measured
missed-due backlog the chosen provider cannot clear, or multi-day durable waits
with human signals the substrate cannot express. This is an architecture
decision with a measurable revisit trigger, not timeless constitutional law.

### RULING 220 — Level-2 scheduling authority persists in a Postgres provider behind the existing control-plane interfaces

*2026-08-30 · author_explicit · `R-0220`*

**The runtime persistence provider for Level-2 scheduling authority is a
Postgres/Neon-backed provider implementing the existing provider-neutral
`ControlPlaneRepositories` interfaces** — a new file beside
`lib/control-plane/repository/file-store.ts`, in a DEDICATED database separate
from the reader-serving Neon database, with schema owned by the provider
itself: outside `lib/db`, outside `drizzle.config.ts`, invisible to
`pnpm db:gate`. Decided by this session under the author's Session A
directive (Work Item 3), which explicitly delegated recording this decision.

**The requirements that decide it.** Level-2 scheduling authority needs shared
claiming across processes AND machines (the primary laptop plus the always-on
secondary); reliable due-time queries at scale; multiple concurrent disposable
workers; survival independent of one laptop's filesystem; and backup/restore.
The filesystem provider's crash/reclaim behavior is genuinely proven — the
Pima shadow run recorded a lease expiring, partial evidence preserved, and a
reclaimed replacement Attempt — but that proof is of the COORDINATOR SEMANTICS
over the interfaces, and a provider-conformance suite carries it to any
provider. What the filesystem cannot carry across is the claim itself: its
`exclusiveCreate`/`link()` lock semantics are single-host and cannot
arbitrate between two machines, and the Drive mirror is an
eventually-consistent synced folder, not a locking substrate. Due-time queries
over a filesystem mean full-directory scans; a SQL index is the boring correct
tool. Neon survives either laptop and has point-in-time restore.

**The file store's "WHY A FILESYSTEM AND NOT A DATABASE" section is honored,
not overruled.** Its arguments were that serving-Postgres residency would trip
RULING 126's domain separation and `pnpm db:gate` — the dedicated database
with provider-owned bootstrap DDL avoids both — and that committed files
already satisfy "survives process death," which is true for one machine, and
Level 2 adds machines. The section itself says swapping the provider later is
a new file in that directory, not a change to a domain rule.

**The migration/adapter plan (Session B executes it; nothing migrates this
session):**

1. `lib/control-plane/repository/pg-store.ts` implementing
   `ControlPlaneRepositories`; idempotent provider-owned bootstrap DDL
   versioned inside the module; connection named by the env var
   WTP_CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL (name only, never a value).
2. Provider conformance: the existing durable-runtime, crash-recovery and
   shadow-run tests parameterized over providers; both providers must pass
   identically — CAS refusals, append-only violations, lock semantics
   (advisory locks / row versioning), lease expiry and reclaim.
3. The due-work surface is designed provider-neutrally at the interface and
   implemented by both providers; the filesystem may implement it naively,
   since it stops being authoritative for scheduling.
4. What moves: NEW Level-2 scheduling state (due-work, freshness debt) is born
   on the Postgres provider. Existing shadow-run state stays in its committed
   filesystem roots as historical evidence — never rewritten. A WorkItem
   needed live under the scheduler is re-registered through the interfaces,
   not file-copied.
5. What stays: the filesystem provider remains fully supported — dev, offline,
   shadow runs, tests — and remains authoritative for everything that is not
   Level-2 scheduling authority until a later recorded decision says
   otherwise.
6. Proof of cutover: the scheduler runs against Postgres from both machines
   with claim contention exercised (two workers, one route, exactly one wins,
   the loser observes the lease conflict); crash/reclaim reproduced on
   Postgres; a backup/restore drill. Only then does the FRESHNESS contract
   stop reading NOT_READY.
7. One control plane throughout: same interfaces, same coordinator, never a
   second state store beside the repositories.

**Revisit trigger** (the same as the no-external-orchestration decision): a
measured missed-due backlog the chosen provider cannot clear, or multi-day
durable waits with human signals the substrate cannot express.

### RULING 289 — PRODUCTION authority accepts a pointer superset from the import receipt

*2026-09-16 · author_explicit · `R-0289`*

**The PRODUCTION authority generation accepts a pointer superset from the import receipt.**

The exact-equality pointer count gate at reader-execution-authority.ts:1362 assumed production is frozen between import and closure. RULING 283 says the opposite — the standing runner promotes continuously by design. Exact parity makes every closure fail on arithmetic the moment the runner does its job.

Accepting a superset keeps the proof honest: the imported pointers are all still there, while production has moved forward. Fewer pointers than the receipt is still a failure — that means something was lost, which is the case the gate should catch.

The same principle extends to the readback verifier code check (line 1198): the standing runner re-verifies pointers with current deployed code, not the original importer code. For PRODUCTION, the verifier code SHA is not required to match the importer code.

---

### RULING 290 — meeting partition versions may advance past the import receipt

*2026-09-16 · author_explicit · `R-0290`*

**The meeting partition version check accepts any promoted version, not only the exact version recorded in the import receipt.**

The import receipt captures a frozen snapshot of production at the moment of the one-time PDC migration. The standing runner (RULING 283) promotes meeting partitions continuously — 79 partitions advanced from their bootstrap `trusted-lkg` versions to real `cv-` civic versions within 24 hours of the import. The exact-version check at snapshot.ts:1030 meant the proof pipeline could only pass if the runner had done nothing since the import, which inverts the design: the runner working correctly was the failure mode.

Every partition in the receipt must still be present and still be promoted. A newer version passes. Missing, unpromoted, or rolled-backward partitions still fail. The disposition check (PROMOTED vs NOT_RECORDED) and the partition membership check are unchanged.
